name: llama.cpp (Metal backend on Apple silicon)
baseline: Core ML LLM conversions running on the Neural Engine (CoreML-LLM)
verdict_reason: llama.cpp out-decodes the Core ML Neural Engine path in the one same-table comparison, but those cells are Debug builds. In release-build cells of the same harness it trails MLX Swift on every row, at roughly half MLX's speed on hybrid Mamba-2 models, and it used the most energy per token on the phone.
tier_reason: Third-party harness with public code; llama.cpp build number and commit, devices and quantization are stated.
claimed_speedup: iPhone 17 Pro, Qwen 3.5 2B: 39.1 vs 27.9 tok/s over Core ML/ANE (Debug builds); slower than MLX Swift elsewhere: 38.8 vs 49.1 tok/s (Gemma 4 E2B, iPhone 17 Pro), 127.1 vs 177.8 tok/s (Gemma 4 E2B, M4 Max), 86.2 vs 159.7 tok/s (Nemotron-3 Nano 30B-A3B, M4 Max); 0.483 J/tok on iPhone, the highest of all runtimes
workload: Batch-1 greedy decoding of Q4_K_M GGUF models: 128-token short-chat on iPhone, llama-bench tg256 after a pp512 prompt for the hybrid models on M4 Max, 600-second sustained run for energy.
hardware: iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro); Apple M4 Max
os: iOS 26.4.2 (Qwen 3.5 2B cells); iOS 27 beta; macOS 27 beta
toolchain: llama.cpp Homebrew build 8680 (commit 15f786e65) for the M4 Max hybrid runs
install: Homebrew, CMake source build, XCFramework for Apple apps
one_liner: C/C++ LLM runtime with a Metal backend; beats Core ML's Neural Engine path on burst decode but trails MLX Swift on Apple silicon.
how_it_is_fast: llama.cpp runs GGUF models through hand-written Metal kernels for quantized matrix-vector products, with k-quant formats such as Q4_K_M that cut memory traffic per token. Weights are memory-mapped, so loading is fast and clean pages are not charged to the app's footprint.
use_it_when: You need one runtime across Apple platforms, Linux, Windows and Android
The model only exists as a GGUF file
Low charged memory footprint matters more than tokens per second (weights are mmap'd)
skip_it_when: Peak decode speed on Apple silicon: MLX Swift was faster on every row of the same harness
Battery-sensitive iPhone apps: it drew the most energy per token and kept the least of its burst rate under sustained load
Google's official Gemma 4 QAT GGUF, which failed to load in this harness
caveats: The only direct Core ML comparison uses Debug-build captures, which the harness's own rules flag
Quantization differs between columns (Q4_K_M vs MLX 4-bit affine)
llama.cpp's own Apple silicon table (discussion #4167) gives absolute llama-bench numbers per chip with no Core ML or MLX baseline
iOS 27 and macOS 27 betas for the newer cells
tradeoffs: Mmap'd weights hide about 2.9 GB of resident memory behind a 191 MB charged footprint on iPhone
C API; Swift apps need a wrapper or the XCFramework
